notes: Compact semantic conjunctions seek by increasing document frequency and score only aligned matches in bounded 128-hit batches. Controls are the original group-capable executor and the candidate-run dense-window experiment.

Ranked plain conjunctions bypass dense score windows. All eligible matching documents are scored; unsupported compositions and complete membership callers retain the general scorer. Union windows retain candidate-run scoring.
The automatic score-required union classification was removed after its prior full-corpus regression. The before control is frozen group-impact-v2, before that experiment.

Explicit per-term statistics are carried through decomposition. Grouping that cannot preserve them retains the original scorer; unsupported L1 backfill rejects instead of changing statistics. Named regression tests reproduced the prior rank and score errors.

No format or scoring formula changes. Both binaries use identical immutable rounded and group-impact indexes. Source changes in this phase must be considered together when interpreting code-generation effects on otherwise unchanged query classes.
Every full cloud archive was downloaded and verified against its external SHA256 and every manifest entry before packaging. This ZIP is also verified entry by entry.
Binaries and raw perf data are omitted from the compact ZIP; full archive hashes, frozen source, locks, adapters, gates, raw latency samples, profiles and memory evidence are retained.
Official timings cover all 962 queries on all 5,032,104 documents. The separate 714-term workload is derived from those queries; it does not change the official query mix.
Every gate compares exact COUNT with Tantivy and pruned Summa top-10/100/1000 ordered IDs and score bits with Summa exhaustive collection. Cross-engine score or ranking identity is not claimed.

Cloud timings use the same Cascade Lake machine, Rust 1.98.1, native CPU optimization, LTO and one query CPU, seven samples after ten-second warmup. ARM timings use the first 100,000 documents, two fixtures, eleven rotated samples and fifteen-second warmup.
Published latency aggregates are geometric means of per-query median microseconds, not pooled-request percentiles.

CPU software sampling, query diagnostics, builds, index audits, hashing and artifact transfers are separate from latency measurements. These results do not establish cold-cache or concurrent-ingest performance.
Document-order binary arrays remain on the machine; archives retain their hashes, lengths and regeneration code. Index files are represented by per-file manifests.
Indexing memory budget is a writer buffer budget, not a limit on process RSS. Heap, mapped file pages and process peak RSS are distinct measurements.
